I'm converting the first section's rows into binary patterns using the two colors present, mapping the minority/majority color to 0/1 to compare against the target section's colors.

Testing both color-mapping candidates against the actual right-side rows for section 1, I find the first mapping (0→7, 1→3) gives far fewer mismatches, so I finalize those rows as 7733, 7377, 7373, 3733, 3777.

Moving to the second section (rows 5-9, colors 3 and 7), I encode each row as bits again and test both mappings against the wrapped-around target colors (1,9), finding the second mapping fits much better with only 2 total mismatches.

I'm mapping the two color pairs to binary digits, translating row0's pattern of 9s and 4s into a 0/1 sequence, then checking if substituting 3 and 8 for those bits reproduces the second section's coloring.

Testing this mapping against the actual right-side rows confirms 4→8, 9→3 works with minimal discrepancy, so I'm applying that rule across all rows of the first section.

Now I'm working through the second section, converting its 3/8 pattern into bits and testing whether 0→9, 1→4 (or the reverse) correctly predicts the corresponding output rows.

Continuing the row checks, r11 also fits the 1→4, 0→9 mapping. Testing this against all rows, r7 through r11 match exactly, with only r6 showing two discrepancies out of seven positions — strong enough evidence that this mapping is correct overall.
